verses.1:1: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
verses.1:2: to the church of God that is at Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, along with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours.
verses.1:3: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: I always give thanks to my God on your behalf for the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:5: that in all things you were made rich in Him, in every word and in all knowledge.
verses.1:6: Just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you,
verses.1:7: so that you lack nothing in any grace, as you await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:8: who will also confirm you all the way to the end, without blame in the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.1:10: Now I plead with you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you say the very same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected in the same mind and in the same judgment.
verses.1:11: For it has been reported to me about you, my brothers, by those who belong to Chloe, that there are contentions among you.
verses.1:12: Now I say this, that each one of you says, "I indeed belong to Paul," "and I to Apollos," "and I to Cephas," "and I to Christ."
verses.1:13: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified on your behalf? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
verses.1:14: I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
verses.1:15: so that no one may say that you were baptized in my name.
verses.1:16: Now I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
verses.1:17: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the gospel, not in wisdom of word, so that the cross of Christ may not be made void.
verses.1:18: For the word of the cross is indeed foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved, that is, to us, it is the power of God.
verses.1:19: For it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will reject the discernment of the discerning."
verses.1:20: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the inquirer of this age? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?
verses.1:21: For since in the wisdom of God the world did not know God through wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.
verses.1:22: For both Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
verses.1:23: but we preach Christ crucified, to Jews indeed a stumbling block, and to the Gentiles foolishness,
verses.1:24: but to those themselves who are called, Jews as well as Greeks, Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God;
verses.1:25: because what is foolish of God is wiser than men, and what is weak of God is stronger than men.
verses.1:26: For look at your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many are powerful, not many are noble;
verses.1:27: but God chose the foolish things of the world so that He might put the wise to shame, and God chose the weak things of the world so that He might put the strong things to shame,
verses.1:28: and God chose the lowly things of the world and the despised things, and the things that are not, so that He might destroy the things that are,
verses.1:29: so that no flesh may boast in His sight.
verses.1:30: Now from Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption,
verses.1:31: so that, just as it is written, "He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord."
verses.2:1: And I, when I came to you, brothers, came not in loftiness of speech or of wisdom, declaring to you the testimony of Christ.
verses.2:2: For I did not judge myself to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.
verses.2:3: And I was with you in weakness, and fear, and much trembling;
verses.2:4: and my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
verses.2:5: so that your faith may not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
verses.2:6: Yet we do speak wisdom among the perfect, though a wisdom not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are being destroyed;
verses.2:7: but we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, which has been hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,
verses.2:8: which none of the rulers of this age knew; for if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.2:9: But just as it is written, "What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor has come up into the heart of man, the things that God has prepared for those who love Him,"
verses.2:10: yet to us God has revealed them through His Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
verses.2:11: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
verses.2:12: Now we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things that have been bestowed on us by God;
verses.2:13: which we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in the teaching of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.
verses.2:14: Now the natural man does not receive the things that are of the Spirit of God, for it is foolishness to him, and he cannot understand it, because it is examined spiritually.
verses.2:15: The spiritual man, however, judges all things, yet he himself is judged by no one.
verses.2:16: For who has known the mind of the Lord, who may instruct Him? Yet we have the mind of Christ.
verses.3:1: And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to fleshly ones. As to infants in Christ,
verses.3:2: I gave you milk to drink, not food, for you were not yet able; nor indeed are you able even now, for you are still fleshly.
verses.3:3: For since there is jealousy and contention among you, are you not fleshly, and do you not walk according to man?
verses.3:4: For when one says, "I indeed belong to Paul," and another, "I to Apollos," are you not men? What then is Apollos? And what is Paul?
verses.3:5: Servants of Him whom you believed, and to each one just as the Lord gave.
verses.3:6: I planted, Apollos watered, yet God gave the growth.
verses.3:7: Therefore neither the one who plants is anything, nor the one who waters, but God, who gives the growth.
verses.3:8: Now the one who plants and the one who waters are one. Yet each one will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
verses.3:9: For we are God's helpers; you are God's field, you are God's building.
verses.3:10: According to the grace of God that was given to me, as a wise architect I laid a foundation, and another builds upon it. Yet let each one see how he builds upon it.
verses.3:11: For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that has been laid, which is Christ Jesus.
verses.3:12: Now if anyone builds upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
verses.3:13: each one's work will be manifest, for the day of the Lord will disclose it, because it will be revealed in fire, and the fire will test what sort each one's work is.
verses.3:14: If anyone's work that he built upon it remains, he will receive a reward.
verses.3:15: If anyone's work burns up, he will suffer loss; but he himself will be saved, yet so as through fire.
verses.3:16: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?
verses.3:17: Now if anyone violates the temple of God, God will destroy him. For the temple of God is holy, which you are.
verses.3:18: Let no one deceive himself: if anyone among you seems to be wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may be wise.
verses.3:19: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, "I will catch the wise in their craftiness."
verses.3:20: And again, "The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty."
verses.3:21: Therefore let no one boast in men.
verses.3:22: For all things are yours, whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; for all things are yours,
verses.3:23: yet you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
verses.4:1: So let a person consider us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
verses.4:2: Now here it is required among stewards that someone be found faithful.
verses.4:3: To me, however, it counts for very little that I should be judged by you or by a human day; yet I do not even judge myself.
verses.4:4: For I am aware of nothing against myself, yet I am not justified by this; rather, the One who judges me is the Lord.
verses.4:5: Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both illuminate the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts; and then there will be praise for each one from God.
verses.4:6: Now these things, brothers, I have applied in a figure to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn that, beyond what is written, one should not be puffed up against another on behalf of another.
verses.4:7: For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? Yet if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
verses.4:8: Already you are satisfied, already you have become rich; without us you reign. And I wish that you did reign, so that we also might reign with you.
verses.4:9: For I think that God has displayed us apostles as last of all, as ones destined for death, because we have been made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to people.
verses.4:10: We are fools on account of Christ, yet you are prudent in Christ; we are weak, yet you are strong; you are noble, yet we are ignoble.
verses.4:11: Up to this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are struck with fists, and are unsettled,
verses.4:12: and we toil, working with our own hands; we are cursed, and we bless; we suffer persecution, and we endure;
verses.4:13: we are slandered, and we plead; we have been made like the sweepings of this world, the dregs of all things until now.
verses.4:14: I am not writing these things to put you to shame, but as my dearest children I admonish you.
verses.4:15: For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, still you do not have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, through the gospel, I fathered you.
verses.4:16: Therefore I appeal to you: be imitators of me, just as I also am of Christ.
verses.4:17: For this reason I have sent Timothy to you, who is my dearest son and faithful in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways that are in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
verses.4:18: As though I were not coming to you, so some have become puffed up.
verses.4:19: However, I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of those who are puffed up, but their power.
verses.4:20: For the kingdom of God is not in talk, but in power.
verses.4:21: What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
verses.5:1: Actually, sexual immorality is heard of among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even among the Gentiles, so that someone has his father's wife.
verses.5:2: And you are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, so that the one who has done this deed may be removed from your midst.
verses.5:3: I indeed, absent in body yet present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, the one who has acted in this way,
verses.5:4: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you and my spirit are gathered together, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
verses.5:5: to hand such a person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.5:6: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump?
verses.5:7: Purge out the old leaven, so that you may be a new batch, just as you are unleavened. For indeed, Christ our Passover has been sacrificed.
verses.5:8: So let us feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and depravity, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
verses.5:9: I wrote in the letter, "Do not associate with sexually immoral people,"
verses.5:10: not at all with the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, or extortioners, or those who serve idols; otherwise you would have had to go out of this world.
verses.5:11: But now I have written to you not to associate: if the one who is named a brother is sexually immoral, or greedy, or one who serves idols, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner, with such a person not even to take food.
verses.5:12: For what is it to me to judge those who are outside? Do you not judge those who are inside?
verses.5:13: For those who are outside, God will judge. Remove the evil from among yourselves.
verses.6:1: Does anyone among you, having a case against another, dare to be judged before the unrighteous and not before the saints?
verses.6:2: Or do you not know that the saints will judge this world? And if the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
verses.6:3: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more secular matters?
verses.6:4: Therefore, if you have secular lawsuits, appoint those who are despised in the church to judge.
verses.6:5: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not any wise person among you who can judge between his brothers?
verses.6:6: Instead, brother contends in a lawsuit with brother, and this before unbelievers?
verses.6:7: Already, indeed, it is altogether a fault in you that you have lawsuits among yourselves. Why do you not rather accept wrong? Why do you not rather suffer fraud?
verses.6:8: Rather, you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and this to brothers.
verses.6:9: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not possess the kingdom of God? Do not be misled: neither sexually immoral people, nor those who serve idols, nor adulterers,
verses.6:10: nor the effeminate, nor those who lie with males, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners will possess the kingdom of God.
verses.6:11: And such were some of you; yet you have been washed, yet you have been sanctified, yet you have been justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
verses.6:12: All things are permitted for me, yet not all things are beneficial; all things are permitted for me, yet I myself will not be brought under the power of anything.
verses.6:13: Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for foods; yet God will destroy both it and them. The body, however, is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
verses.6:14: Moreover, God both raised up the Lord and will raise us up through His power.
verses.6:15: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Taking the members of Christ, then, shall I make them members of a prostitute? Far from it.
verses.6:16: Or do you not know that the one who clings to a prostitute becomes one body? For it says, "The two will be in one flesh."
verses.6:17: But the one who clings to the Lord is one spirit.
verses.6:18: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin, whatever a person commits, is outside the body; but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
verses.6:19: Or do you not know that your members are a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?
verses.6:20: For you were bought at a great price. Glorify and carry God in your body.
verses.7:1: Now regarding the matters you wrote to me about: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
verses.7:2: Yet because of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
verses.7:3: Let the husband pay what is due to his wife, and likewise the wife also to her husband.
verses.7:4: The wife holds no power over her own body, but the husband does. And likewise the husband also holds no power over his own body, but the wife does.
verses.7:5: Do not deprive each other, except perhaps by consent for a time, so that you may be free for prayer; and return together again, so that Satan may not tempt you on account of your lack of self-restraint.
verses.7:6: Now I say this as a concession, not as a command.
verses.7:7: For I wish all of you to be as I myself am; but each one has a gift of his own from God, one in this way, and another in that.
verses.7:8: Now I say to the unmarried and to widows: it is good for them if they remain this way, just as I also do.
verses.7:9: But if they do not practice self-restraint, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn.
verses.7:10: Now to those who are joined in marriage, I command, not I but the Lord, that a wife must not separate from her husband.
verses.7:11: Yet if she does separate, she is to remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
verses.7:12: For to the rest I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to live with him, let him not divorce her.
verses.7:13: And if any believing woman has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to live with her, let her not divorce her husband.
verses.7:14: For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified through the believing wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified through the believing husband; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
verses.7:15: But if the unbeliever separates, let him separate; for a brother or sister is not subjected to bondage in such cases, yet God has called us in peace.
verses.7:16: For how do you know, wife, if you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, if you will save your wife?
verses.7:17: Only, as the Lord has apportioned to each one, as God has called each one, so let him walk, and just as I teach in all the churches.
verses.7:18: Was anyone called circumcised? Let him not draw forward the foreskin. Was anyone called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
verses.7:19: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but rather the keeping of God's commandments.
verses.7:20: Let each person remain in that calling in which he was called.
verses.7:21: Were you called a slave? Do not let it be a concern to you; yet even if you are able to become free, rather make use of it.
verses.7:22: For the one who was called a slave in the Lord is a freedman of the Lord; likewise, the one who was called free is a slave of Christ.
verses.7:23: You were purchased at a price; do not become slaves of human beings.
verses.7:24: Brothers, let each one remain with God in that in which he was called.
verses.7:25: Now regarding virgins, I do not have a command of the Lord, yet I give counsel as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
verses.7:26: Therefore I consider this to be good because of the pressing necessity, that it is good for a man to be this way.
verses.7:27: Are you bound to a wife? Do not look for release. Are you released from a wife? Do not look for a wife.
verses.7:28: Yet if you take a wife, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned; still, such people will have affliction of the flesh. And I am sparing you.
verses.7:29: Therefore I say this, brothers: the time is short. What remains is that even those who have wives should be as though having none;
verses.7:30: and those who weep, as though not weeping; and those who rejoice, as though not rejoicing; and those who buy, as though not possessing;
verses.7:31: and those who use this world, as though they were not using it; for the shape of this world is passing away.
verses.7:32: Now I want you to be free from concern. The one who is without a wife is concerned with the things of the Lord, how he may please God.
verses.7:33: Yet the one who is with a wife is concerned with the things of the world, how he may please his wife, and he is divided.
verses.7:34: And the unmarried woman, as well as the virgin, gives thought to the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy in body and in spirit. But the one who is married gives thought to the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
verses.7:35: Furthermore, I say this for your own benefit, not to throw a snare over you, but for what is honorable and for what affords the opportunity to implore the Lord without hindrance.
verses.7:36: Now if anyone thinks he appears dishonorable regarding his virgin because she is past her prime, and so it ought to be done, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin if she marries.
verses.7:37: For the one who has resolved steadfastly in his heart, having no necessity, yet having power over his own will, and has decided this in his heart, to keep his virgin, does well.
verses.7:38: Therefore, both the one who joins his virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not join her in marriage does better.
verses.7:39: A wife is bound to the law for as long as her husband lives; yet if her husband falls asleep, she is set free: let her marry whomever she wishes, only in the Lord.
verses.7:40: Yet she will be more blessed if she remains this way, according to my counsel; and I suppose that I also have the Spirit of God.
verses.8:1: Now regarding the things that are sacrificed to idols, we know that all of us have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, whereas love builds up.
verses.8:2: Yet if anyone considers himself to know something, he has not yet known in what way he ought to know.
verses.8:3: Yet if anyone loves God, this one is known by Him.
verses.8:4: Now regarding the foods that are offered in sacrifice to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God except one.
verses.8:5: For even if there are those who are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (since indeed there are many gods and many lords),
verses.8:6: yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we for Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him.
verses.8:7: Yet knowledge is not in everyone. Some, however, with conscience of the idol up to now, eat it as something sacrificed to an idol; and their conscience, since it is weak, is defiled.
verses.8:8: Now food does not commend us to God. For neither if we eat will we abound, nor if we do not eat will we fall short.
verses.8:9: Be careful, however, that this freedom of yours does not perhaps become a stumbling block for the weak.
verses.8:10: For if someone sees the one who has knowledge reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, since it is weak, be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?
verses.8:11: And will the weak one perish by your knowledge, the brother for whom Christ died?
verses.8:12: Yet by sinning in this way against the brothers, and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
verses.8:13: For this reason, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will not eat meat ever again, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.
verses.9:1: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Christ Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
verses.9:2: And if I am not an apostle to others, yet still I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
verses.9:3: My defense before those who question me is this:
verses.9:4: Do we not have the right to eat and to drink?
verses.9:5: Do we not have the right to take around with us a woman who is a sister, just as the rest of the apostles also do, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
verses.9:6: Or do only I and Barnabas not have the right to do this?
verses.9:7: Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat from its fruit? Who shepherds a flock and does not eat from the milk of the flock?
verses.9:8: Am I saying these things according to man? Or does the law not also say these things?
verses.9:9: For it is written in the law of Moses, "You shall not bind the mouth of a threshing ox." Is God concerned about oxen?
verses.9:10: Or does He certainly say this for our sake? For these things were written for our sake, because the one who plows ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes, in hope of receiving the fruit.
verses.9:11: If we have sown spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap your material things?
verses.9:12: If others share in the right over you, why not we all the more? Yet we have not used this right, but we endure all things, so that we may not give any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.
verses.9:13: Do you not know that those who work in the sanctuary eat the things that are from the sanctuary, and those who serve at the altar share with the altar?
verses.9:14: In this way the Lord also ordained for those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.
verses.9:15: But I have used none of these things. And I have not written these things so that they should be done this way in my case, for it is better for me to die than for anyone to make my glory void.
verses.9:16: For if I preach the gospel, there is no glory for me, because a necessity presses upon me; for woe to me if I do not preach the gospel.
verses.9:17: For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, a stewardship has been entrusted to me.
verses.9:18: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may present the gospel free of charge, so that I do not misuse my right in the gospel.
verses.9:19: For though I was free from all, I made myself the slave of all, so that I might gain more.
verses.9:20: And to the Jews I became like a Jew, so that I might gain the Jews;
verses.9:21: to those who are under the law, as though I were under the law (though I myself was not under the law), so that I might gain those who were under the law; to those who were without the law, as though I were without the law (though I was not without the law of God, but was in the law of Christ), so that I might gain those who were without the law.
verses.9:22: To the weak I became weak, so that I might gain the weak. To all I have become all things, so that I might save all.
verses.9:23: And I do all things on account of the gospel, so that I may become a sharer in it.
verses.9:24: Do you not know that those who run in a stadium all indeed run, yet one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may lay hold of it.
verses.9:25: Now everyone who competes in a contest abstains from all things; and they indeed do so that they may receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one.
verses.9:26: I therefore run in this way, not as though toward something uncertain; I fight in this way, not as though beating the air;
verses.9:27: but I chastise my body and bring it into servitude, so that after I have preached to others, I myself may not somehow become disqualified.
verses.10:1: For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all crossed through the sea,
verses.10:2: and all were baptized in Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
verses.10:3: and all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.10:4: and all drank the same spiritual drink (for they were drinking from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ);
verses.10:5: yet God was not well pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the desert.
verses.10:6: Now these things happened as a figure for us, so that we might not be desiring evil things, just as they also desired.
verses.10:7: And do not become idolaters, as some of them were, just as it is written, "The people sat down to eat and to drink, and they rose up to play."
verses.10:8: And let us not practice sexual immorality, as some of them practiced it, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
verses.10:9: And let us not put Christ to the test, as some of them put Him to the test, and perished by serpents.
verses.10:10: And do not grumble, as some of them grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.
verses.10:11: Now all these things happened to them as a figure, and they were written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
verses.10:12: Therefore let the one who thinks he is standing watch out that he does not fall.
verses.10:13: Let no temptation seize you except what is human; yet God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make a way out, so that you may be able to endure it.
verses.10:14: For this reason, my dearly beloved, flee from the worship of idols.
verses.10:15: I speak as to prudent people; you yourselves judge what I say.
verses.10:16: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a communion in the blood of Christ? And the bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of the Lord?
verses.10:17: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, all of us who partake of the one bread.
verses.10:18: Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices partakers of the altar?
verses.10:19: What then? Am I saying that what has been sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
verses.10:20: Rather, the things that the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not want you to become partners with demons.
verses.10:21: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
verses.10:22: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He? All things are permitted for me, yet not all things are beneficial.
verses.10:23: All things are permitted for me, yet not all things build up.
verses.10:24: Let no one seek what is his own, but what belongs to another.
verses.10:25: Eat everything that is sold in the meat market, asking nothing on account of conscience.
verses.10:26: The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness.
verses.10:27: If anyone among the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat everything that is set before you, asking nothing on account of conscience.
verses.10:28: But if someone says, "This has been sacrificed to idols," do not eat, on account of the one who pointed it out, and on account of conscience.
verses.10:29: By conscience, however, I mean not your own, but another's. For why is my freedom judged by someone else's conscience?
verses.10:30: If I partake with gratitude, why am I reviled over that for which I give thanks?
verses.10:31: Therefore, whether you eat, or drink, or do anything else, do all things for the glory of God.
verses.10:32: Be without offense to Jews, and to Gentiles, and to the church of God,
verses.10:33: just as I also please everyone in all things, not seeking what is advantageous to myself, but what is for many, so that they may be saved.
verses.11:1: Be imitators of me, just as I too am of Christ.
verses.11:2: Now I praise you, brothers, because in all things you are mindful of me and hold to my precepts just as I handed them down to you.
verses.11:3: Yet I want you to know that every man's head is Christ, while woman's head is man, and Christ's head is God.
verses.11:4: Every man praying or prophesying with a veiled head disgraces his head.
verses.11:5: Yet every woman praying or prophesying with an unveiled head disgraces her head, for it is one and the same as if she were shaved bald.
verses.11:6: For if a woman is not veiled, let her be shorn. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to be shorn or shaved bald, let her veil her head.
verses.11:7: A man indeed ought not to veil his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
verses.11:8: For man is not from woman, but woman from man.
verses.11:9: For indeed, man was not created for the sake of woman, but woman for the sake of man.
verses.11:10: Therefore a woman ought to have authority on her head because of the angels.
verses.11:11: Nevertheless, neither is man without woman, nor woman without man, in the Lord.
verses.11:12: For just as woman is from man, so also is man through woman; yet all things are from God.
verses.11:13: You yourselves judge: is it fitting for an unveiled woman to pray to God?
verses.11:14: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man indeed grows long hair, it is a dishonor to him,
verses.11:15: whereas if a woman grows long hair, it is a glory to her? For her hair has been given to her in place of a veil.
verses.11:16: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor does the church of God.
verses.11:17: Now this I command, not giving praise, because you come together not for the better, but for the worse.
verses.11:18: First indeed, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
verses.11:19: For there must also be heresies, so that those too who are approved may become manifest among you.
verses.11:20: Therefore, when you come together into one place, it is no longer to eat the Lord's supper.
verses.11:21: For each one takes his own supper beforehand to eat, and one indeed is hungry, while another is drunk.
verses.11:22: Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the church of God and put to shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Do I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
verses.11:23: For I received from the Lord what I also handed down to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was being handed over, took bread,
verses.11:24: and giving thanks, He broke it and said, "Take and eat: this is My body, which will be handed over for you. Do this in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:25: Similarly He took the cup also, after He had eaten supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:26: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you will proclaim the death of the Lord until He comes.
verses.11:27: Therefore, whoever eats this bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
verses.11:28: But let a person examine himself, and in this way let him eat from that bread and drink from the cup.
verses.11:29: For the one who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment for himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.
verses.11:30: For this reason many among you are weak and sickly, and many sleep.
verses.11:31: But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would certainly not be judged.
verses.11:32: Yet while we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, so that we may not be condemned with this world.
verses.11:33: So then, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
verses.11:34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you may not come together for judgment. And the rest I will set in order when I come.
verses.12:1: Now concerning spiritual things, I do not want you to be unaware, brothers.
verses.12:2: You know that when you were Gentiles, you went to mute idols just as you were being led.
verses.12:3: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, "Anathema to Jesus," and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except in the Holy Spirit.
verses.12:4: Now there are distributions of graces, but the same Spirit;
verses.12:5: and there are distributions of ministries, but the same Lord;
verses.12:6: and there are distributions of workings, yet the same God, who works all things in all.
verses.12:7: Now to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for benefit.
verses.12:8: To one indeed through the Spirit is given an utterance of wisdom, and to another an utterance of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
verses.12:9: to another faith in the same Spirit; to another the grace of healings in the one Spirit;
verses.12:10: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of utterances.
verses.12:11: Now one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each individually just as He wills.
verses.12:12: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though they are many, are yet one body, so also is Christ.
verses.12:13: For indeed, in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether slaves or free, and we were all made to drink in one Spirit.
verses.12:14: For the body also is not one member, but many.
verses.12:15: If the foot says, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body?
verses.12:16: And if the ear says, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," is it therefore of the body?
verses.12:17: If the whole body were an eye, where would hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would smelling be?
verses.12:18: But now God has placed the members, each one of them in the body, just as He willed.
verses.12:19: And if all were one member, where would the body be?
verses.12:20: But now there are indeed many members, yet one body.
verses.12:21: And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of your service," or again the head to the feet, "You are not necessary to me."
verses.12:22: But much more, those members of the body that seem to be weaker are more necessary;
verses.12:23: and those members of the body that we consider less noble, around these we place more abundant honor; and our unseemly parts have more abundant seemliness.
verses.12:24: But our seemly parts have need of nothing; instead, God has tempered the body, by granting more abundant honor to that which lacked it,
verses.12:25: so that there may be no schism in the body, but that the members may have the very same care for one another.
verses.12:26: And if one member suffers anything, all the members suffer with it; or if one member glories, all the members rejoice with it.
verses.12:27: Now you are the body of Christ, and members of a member.
verses.12:28: And God has indeed placed some in the church: first, apostles; second, prophets; next, teachers; then, miracles; after that, graces of healings, helps, administrations, kinds of tongues, interpretations of utterances.
verses.12:29: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers?
verses.12:30: Do all perform miracles? Do all have the grace of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
verses.12:31: Now eagerly seek the better gifts. And I point out to you a still more excellent way.
verses.13:1: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, yet do not have love, I have become like resounding bronze or a ringing cymbal.
verses.13:2: And if I have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, yet do not have love, I am nothing.
verses.13:3: And if I distribute all my possessions for the food of the poor, and if I hand over my body so that I may burn, yet do not have love, it benefits me nothing.
verses.13:4: Love is patient; it is kind. Love is not envious, does not act wrongly, is not puffed up,
verses.13:5: is not ambitious, does not seek what is its own, is not irritated, does not think evil,
verses.13:6: does not rejoice over injustice, but rejoices together with the truth;
verses.13:7: it bears everything, believes everything, hopes for everything, endures everything.
verses.13:8: Love never falls away, whether prophecies will be done away with, or tongues will cease, or knowledge will be destroyed.
verses.13:9: For in part we know, and in part we prophesy.
verses.13:10: But when what is perfect has come, what is in part will be done away with.
verses.13:11: When I was a little child, I spoke like a little child, I understood like a little child, I thought like a little child. Yet when I became a man, I did away with the things that belonged to a little child.
verses.13:12: We see now through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know just as I also have been known.
verses.13:13: But now there remain faith, hope, love, these three; yet the greatest of these is love.
verses.14:1: Pursue love, be eager for spiritual things, yet even more that you may prophesy.
verses.14:2: For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God, for no one hears; yet in spirit he speaks mysteries.
verses.14:3: For the one who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and encouragement, and comfort.
verses.14:4: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church of God.
verses.14:5: Now I want you all to speak in tongues, yet even more to prophesy. For the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless perhaps he interprets so that the church may receive edification.
verses.14:6: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what benefit will I be to you unless I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in teaching?
verses.14:7: Yet things without life that give sound, whether flute or lyre, unless they give a distinction of tones, how will it be known what is played on the flute or what is played on the lyre?
verses.14:8: For indeed, if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare himself for war?
verses.14:9: So also you, unless by the tongue you give clear speech, how will it be known what is said? For you will be speaking into the air.
verses.14:10: There are, for example, so many kinds of languages in this world, and nothing is without a voice.
verses.14:11: If therefore I do not know the meaning of the voice, I will be a foreigner to the one to whom I speak, and the one who speaks will be a foreigner to me.
verses.14:12: So also you, since you are zealous for spirits, seek to abound for the edification of the church.
verses.14:13: And therefore let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
verses.14:14: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is without fruit.
verses.14:15: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing psalms with the spirit, and I will also sing psalms with the mind.
verses.14:16: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will the one who fills the place of an uninstructed person say "Amen" upon your blessing, since he does not know what you are saying?
verses.14:17: For you indeed give thanks well, but the other person is not edified.
verses.14:18: I give thanks to my God that I speak in the tongue of all of you.
verses.14:19: Yet in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, so that I may instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verses.14:20: Brothers, do not become children in your understanding, but in malice be little children; in your understanding, however, be mature.
verses.14:21: In the law it is written, "In other tongues and with other lips I will speak to this people, and not even so will they listen to Me," says the Lord.
verses.14:22: Therefore tongues are for a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers; prophecies, however, are not for unbelievers, but for believers.
verses.14:23: If therefore the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed persons or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are insane?
verses.14:24: But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or uninstructed person enters, he is convicted by all, he is judged by all.
verses.14:25: The hidden things of his heart become manifest, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God, declaring that God is truly among you.
verses.14:26: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
verses.14:27: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two, or at the most three, and in turn, and one interprets.
verses.14:28: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church; instead, let him speak to himself and to God.
verses.14:29: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the rest judge.
verses.14:30: But if something is revealed to another who is seated, let the first keep silent.
verses.14:31: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged.
verses.14:32: And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
verses.14:33: For God is not a God of dissension, but of peace, just as I also teach in all the churches of the saints.
verses.14:34: Let women keep silent in the churches, for it is not permitted for them to speak, but to be submissive, just as the law also says.
verses.14:35: But if they want to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home. For it is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
verses.14:36: Or did the word of God come forth from you? Or did it reach you alone?
verses.14:37: If anyone seems to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize that the things I write to you are the Lord's commands.
verses.14:38: But if anyone does not know, he will not be known.
verses.14:39: Therefore, brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
verses.14:40: Yet let all things be done properly and according to order.
verses.15:1: Now, brothers, I make known to you the gospel that I preached to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
verses.15:2: through which you are also being saved, if you hold fast to the manner in which I preached to you, unless you believed in vain.
verses.15:3: For I handed down to you first of all what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:4: and that He was buried, and that He rose on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:5: and that He was seen by Cephas, and after this by the eleven;
verses.15:6: then He was seen by more than five hundred brothers together, of whom many remain until now, though some have fallen asleep;
verses.15:7: then He was seen by James, then by all the apostles;
verses.15:8: and last of all, as by one born prematurely, He was seen by me also.
verses.15:9: For I myself am the least of the apostles, one who is not worthy to be called an apostle, since I persecuted the church of God.
verses.15:10: Yet by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace in me was not empty, but I labored more abundantly than all of them; not I, however, but the grace of God with me.
verses.15:11: For whether it is I or they, thus we preach, and thus you believed.
verses.15:12: But if Christ is preached, that He has risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.15:13: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen.
verses.15:14: And if Christ has not risen, then our preaching is empty, and your faith is empty as well.
verses.15:15: And we are also found to be false witnesses of God, since we bore witness against God that He raised Christ, whom He did not raise, if the dead do not rise.
verses.15:16: For if the dead do not rise, neither has Christ risen.
verses.15:17: And if Christ has not risen, your faith is futile; for you are still in your sins.
verses.15:18: Therefore those who have fallen asleep in Christ have also perished.
verses.15:19: If in this life only we are hoping in Christ, we are more pitiable than all people.
verses.15:20: But now Christ has risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep,
verses.15:21: since indeed through a man came death, and through a man the resurrection of the dead.
verses.15:22: And just as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will also be made alive.
verses.15:23: But each one in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; then those who belong to Christ, who have believed in His coming.
verses.15:24: Then the end, when He delivers the kingdom to God and the Father, when He has nullified every rule and authority and power.
verses.15:25: Now He must reign until He places all enemies under His feet.
verses.15:26: And as the last enemy, death will be destroyed; for He has subjected all things under His feet. But when He says,
verses.15:27: "All things have been subjected to Him," without doubt this excludes Him who subjected all things to Him.
verses.15:28: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then even the Son Himself will be subjected to Him who subjected all things to Him, so that God may be all in all.
verses.15:29: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized for the dead, if the dead do not rise at all? Why are they even baptized for them?
verses.15:30: Why do we also face danger every hour?
verses.15:31: I die daily, by your glory, brothers, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.15:32: If in human terms I fought against wild beasts at Ephesus, what does it benefit me, if the dead do not rise? "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
verses.15:33: Do not be led astray: bad conversations corrupt good morals.
verses.15:34: Wake up, you righteous, and do not sin; for some have ignorance of God. To your shame I speak to you.
verses.15:35: But someone will say, "How do the dead rise? Or with what kind of body will they come?"
verses.15:36: Foolish one, what you yourself sow is not made alive unless it first dies;
verses.15:37: and what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but a bare grain, for instance of wheat or of one of the others.
verses.15:38: But God gives it a body as He wills, just as to each of the seeds its own body.
verses.15:39: Not all flesh is the same flesh, but one kind is of humans, another of livestock, another of birds, and another of fish.
verses.15:40: There are both heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, yet one is the glory of the heavenly, and another is that of the earthly.
verses.15:41: One is the brightness of the sun, another the brightness of the moon, and another the brightness of the stars; for star differs from star in brightness.
verses.15:42: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it will rise in incorruption.
verses.15:43: It is sown in dishonor; it will rise in glory. It is sown in weakness; it will rise in power.
verses.15:44: It is sown a natural body; it will rise a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual one, as it is written:
verses.15:45: "The first man Adam was made into a living soul"; the last Adam, into a life-giving spirit.
verses.15:46: Yet what is spiritual is not first, but what is natural; then what is spiritual.
verses.15:47: The first man is from the earth, earthly; the second man is from heaven, heavenly.
verses.15:48: As is the earthly one, such also are the earthly; and as is the heavenly one, such also are the heavenly.
verses.15:49: Therefore, just as we have borne the image of the earthly one, let us also bear the image of the heavenly one.
verses.15:50: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God, nor will corruption possess incorruptibility.
verses.15:51: Look, I tell you a mystery: we will indeed all rise, but we will not all be changed.
verses.15:52: In a moment, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, and we will be changed.
verses.15:53: For it is necessary for this corruptible to put on incorruption, and for this mortal to put on immortality.
verses.15:54: And when this mortal has put on immortality, then the word that is written will come about: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
verses.15:55: "Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?"
verses.15:56: And the sting of death is sin, while the power of sin is the law.
verses.15:57: But thanks be to God, who gave us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:58: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be firm and immovable, abounding in the work of the Lord always, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.
verses.16:1: Now regarding the collections that are being made for the saints, just as I instructed the churches of Galatia, you also do so.
verses.16:2: On each first day of the week, let each one of you put aside at home, storing up whatever pleases him well, so that when I come, collections will not be made then.
verses.16:3: And when I am present, those whom you approve by letters, these I will send to deliver your gift to Jerusalem.
verses.16:4: And if it is fitting that I also go, they will go with me.
verses.16:5: Now I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I will pass through Macedonia.
verses.16:6: And with you I will perhaps stay, or even spend the winter, so that you may see me on my way wherever I go.
verses.16:7: For I do not want to see you now in passing, for I hope to stay with you for a little while, if the Lord permits.
verses.16:8: I will remain in Ephesus, however, until Pentecost.
verses.16:9: For a great and evident door has been opened to me, and there are many adversaries.
verses.16:10: Now if Timothy comes, see to it that he is without fear among you, for he does the work of the Lord, just as I also do.
verses.16:11: Therefore let no one despise him, but see him on his way in peace so that he may come to me, for I am waiting for him with the brothers.
verses.16:12: Now regarding Apollos the brother, I make known to you that I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, and there was certainly no will that he should come now; but he will come when he has free time.
verses.16:13: Keep watch, stand in the faith, act like men, and be strengthened.
verses.16:14: Let everything you do be done in love.
verses.16:15: Now I implore you, brothers (you know the household of Stephanas, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia and have committed themselves to the service of the saints),
verses.16:16: that you also be subject to people of this kind, and to everyone who works together and labors.
verses.16:17: Now I rejoice at the presence of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they themselves have supplied what was lacking from you.
verses.16:18: For they refreshed both my spirit and yours. Recognize, therefore, those who are of this kind.
verses.16:19: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla, together with their household church, greet you warmly in the Lord; with them I am also lodging.
verses.16:20: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.16:21: The greeting is by my own hand, Paul's.
verses.16:22: If anyone does not love our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Maran Atha.
verses.16:23: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
verses.16:24: My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

notes.1:7: The Vulgate renders Greek charisma ("spiritual gift") as gratia ("grace"), using the same Latin word that appears in verses 3 and 4.
notes.1:8: The Clementine Vulgate adds adventus ("of the coming"), whereas Greek manuscripts read simply "in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ."
notes.1:18: The Vulgate inserts the explanatory gloss id est nobis ("that is, to us") to clarify the Greek phrasing "to us who are being saved."
notes.1:20: The Vulgate includes hujus ("this") before mundi ("world"), matching the majority Greek text against critical editions, and distinguishes hujus saeculi ("of this age") from hujus mundi ("of this world").
notes.2:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads testimonium Christi ("the testimony of Christ"), whereas Greek manuscripts read "the mystery of God" or "the testimony of God."
notes.2:4: The Vulgate includes humanae ("human") and verbis ("words"), agreeing with the majority Greek text where critical editions omit both terms.
notes.2:8: The Vulgate adds emphasis with numquam ("never"), where the Greek text has simply "not."
notes.2:13: Latin spiritualibus (like Greek pneumatikois) can be understood as neuter ("with spiritual things") or masculine ("to spiritual people"), and Vulgate comparantes ("comparing") translates Greek synkrinontes ("interpreting/combining/comparing").
notes.2:14: Latin animalis (from anima, "soul/natural life") renders Greek psychikos and denotes a person governed only by natural human faculties rather than by the Spirit of God.
notes.3:4: In the Clementine Vulgate the questions "What then is Apollos? And what is Paul?" close verse 4, whereas modern Greek-based editions place them at the beginning of verse 5.
notes.3:5: The Vulgate reads ministri ejus, cui credidistis ("Servants of Him whom you believed"), a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek text has "servants through whom you believed."
notes.3:9: The Vulgate renders Greek synergoi ("fellow workers") as adjutores ("helpers" or "assistants").
notes.3:13: The Clementine Vulgate adds Domini ("of the Lord") to "the day," whereas the Greek text reads simply "the day."
notes.3:19: The Vulgate renders the quotation of Job 5:13 in the first-person future (Comprehendam, "I will catch") as direct divine speech, whereas the Greek and Hebrew use a third-person participle ("He who catches").
notes.4:3: Literally "by a human day" (ab humano die), an idiom for a human tribunal or day of human judgment, contrasted with the Lord's judgment in vv. 4-5.
notes.4:6: Unlike the Greek, which separates the maxim "not beyond what is written" from a second-person plural clause, the Vulgate combines them into a single third-person singular clause; transfiguravi literally means "applied in a figure."
notes.4:13: The Vulgate retains the Greek loanword peripsema (literally scrapings, offscouring, or dregs) and specifies "this world" (hujus mundi) where the Greek has simply "the world."
notes.4:16: The closing clause "just as I also am of Christ" (sicut et ego Christi) is a distinctly Vulgate reading (cf. 1 Cor 11:1) absent from the standard critical Greek text.
notes.5:4: The Vulgate has fuller titles in v. 4a ("our Lord Jesus Christ") and v. 5 ("the day of our Lord Jesus Christ") where the critical Greek text has shorter forms (in v. 5 simply "the day of the Lord").
notes.5:6: The Vulgate reads corrumpit ("corrupts" or "spoils"), a distinctive Western reading where the standard Greek text has "leavens" (zymoi).
notes.5:9: The Clementine Vulgate omits "to you" (vobis) here, reading simply "I wrote in the letter," unlike v. 11 and the Greek text.
notes.5:13: The Vulgate reads the future tense judicabit ("will judge"); malum can grammatically be masculine ("the evil person") or neuter ("the evil").
notes.6:4: Latin constituite ("appoint") is an imperative; the Greek form kathizete can be read either as an imperative or as an indicative.
notes.6:5: The Latin literally reads the singular "between his brother" (inter fratrem suum), a compressed idiom meaning between one brother and another.
notes.6:9: Latin possidebunt ("will possess") renders the Greek verb for "inherit" in vv. 9-10, and the Latin verse break falls before neque molles; in v. 10, molles literally means "soft ones" and masculorum concubitores "those who lie with males."
notes.6:19: A distinctly Vulgate plural reading: "your members are a temple" (membra vestra, templum sunt), where the Greek text has singular "your body."
notes.6:20: The Vulgate preserves two distinctive readings absent from the critical Greek text: "at a great price" (pretio magno) and the added command "and carry/bear" (et portate) before "God."
notes.7:7: The Clementine Vulgate reads omnes vos ("all of you"), whereas the Greek text reads pantas anthropous ("all people/men").
notes.7:18: Latin adducat praeputium literally means "draw forward the foreskin," referring to the ancient practice of epispasm (attempting to conceal or reverse circumcision); in the next clause and v. 19, praeputium denotes the state of uncircumcision.
notes.7:21: Latin magis utere ("rather make use of it") leaves the object unstated, preserving the debated ambiguity between taking advantage of the opportunity for freedom and making use of one's present calling.
notes.7:35: Vulgate facultatem praebeat sine impedimento Dominum obsecrandi ("affords the opportunity to implore the Lord without hindrance") differs from the Greek text, which speaks of undistracted attendance or devotion to the Lord.
notes.7:36: The Vulgate reads the singular conditional si nubat ("if she marries") rather than the Greek plural imperative gameitosan ("let them marry"), and keeps "his virgin" open to either an unmarried daughter in a father's care or a betrothed virgin.
notes.8:4: The Vulgate reads De escis ("regarding the foods"), whereas the Greek text reads peri tes broseos ("concerning the eating").
notes.8:7: The Vulgate reads cum conscientia ... idoli ("with conscience of the idol"), reflecting Greek manuscripts with syneidesei ("conscience/awareness") rather than the critical Greek text's synetheia ("habit/being accustomed").
notes.8:8: The Vulgate uses the present tense commendat ("does not commend") and reverses the order of the conditional clauses compared to the critical Greek text, placing eating before not eating.
notes.8:10: The Vulgate reads third-person eum, qui habet scientiam ("the one who has knowledge") instead of Greek second-person "you who have knowledge," and uses aedificabitur ("be built up") in ironic echo of aedificat ("builds up") in 8:1.
notes.9:5: Latin mulierem sororem literally means "a woman, a sister" (since mulier can denote either "woman" or "wife"); interpreters debate whether Paul refers to a Christian wife or to a devout Christian woman assisting the apostles in ministry.
notes.9:6: The Vulgate distinctively reads hoc operandi ("to do this"), referring back to the rights just listed, whereas Greek manuscripts read me ergazesthai ("to refrain from working").
notes.9:15: Here and in 9:16, Latin gloria ("glory") renders Greek kauchema ("boast" or "ground for boasting"); the Vulgate also smooths the abrupt Greek break in 9:15 into a complete comparative clause ("than for anyone to make my glory void").
notes.9:22: The Vulgate distinctively reads ut omnes facerem salvos ("so that I might save all"), whereas Greek manuscripts read hina pantos tinas soso ("that by all means I might save some").
notes.9:27: Latin reprobus literally means "disapproved" or "rejected" after testing, here rendered "disqualified" in keeping with the athletic contest imagery of 9:24-27.
notes.10:13: The Vulgate uniquely uses the subjunctive apprehendat ("Let no temptation seize you"), expressing a wish or warning, whereas Greek manuscripts use the perfect indicative eilephen ("No temptation has overtaken you").
notes.10:16: The Vulgate distinctively reads corporis Domini ("the body of the Lord") rather than the Greek "body of Christ," and renders Greek koinonia with two distinct nouns: communicatio ("communion") for the cup and participatio ("participation") for the bread.
notes.10:17: Latin Quoniam unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus can also be read without an implied verb as "For we who are many are one bread, one body"; the Vulgate also omits "for" (Greek gar) in the closing clause, forming a relative clause ("all of us who partake").
notes.10:22: In the Clementine Vulgate verse division, the first maxim ("All things are permitted for me, yet not all things are beneficial") belongs to 10:22 rather than 10:23, and both verses include mihi ("for me"), absent from the oldest Greek manuscripts.
notes.10:26: The Clementine Vulgate omits an introductory "For" (Greek gar) at the start of this quotation from Psalm 24:1 (Vulgate 23:1).
notes.11:2: The Vulgate reads "my precepts" (praecepta mea) and includes "brothers" (fratres), whereas the critical Greek text has simply "the traditions" without "my" or "brothers."
notes.11:10: Latin potestatem supra caput is literally "authority over the head"; "her" is supplied in English.
notes.11:16: The Vulgate reads the singular "church of God" (ecclesia Dei), whereas the Greek text has the plural ("churches of God").
notes.11:24: The Vulgate includes "Take and eat" (Accipite, et manducate) and reads the future passive "which will be handed over for you" (quod pro vobis tradetur), differing from both the critical Greek text ("which is for you") and the Textus Receptus ("which is broken for you").
notes.11:29: The Vulgate retains "unworthily" (indigne) and "of the Lord" (Domini) in "the body of the Lord," readings absent from the critical Greek text.
notes.12:3: The Vulgate phrase anathema Jesu uses the dative ("anathema / a curse to Jesus"), and the verbless Dominus Jesus functions as the confession "Jesus is Lord" (literally "Lord Jesus").
notes.12:13: The Vulgate reads in uno Spiritu potati sumus ("we were all made to drink in one Spirit"), using the ablative with in, whereas the Greek text has "made to drink one Spirit" in the accusative.
notes.12:16: The Clementine Vulgate omits non before est (literally "is it therefore of the body?"), unlike v. 15 (num ideo non est de corpore?), the Greek text, and critical Vulgate editions, which include the negation.
notes.12:27: The Vulgate reads membra de membro ("members of a member," reflecting a Greek variant ek melous), whereas most Greek manuscripts read ek merous ("individually" or "in part").
notes.12:28: The Vulgate reads exinde ("next") rather than "third" before "teachers," and adds interpretationes sermonum ("interpretations of utterances") at the end of the verse, an addition absent from the Greek text.
notes.13:3: The Vulgate explicitly reads 'for the food of the poor' (in cibos pauperum) and 'so that I may burn' (ita ut ardeam), reflecting the Greek variant kauthesomai rather than kauchesomai ('so that I may boast').
notes.13:4: Latin non agit perperam literally means 'does not act wrongly' or 'perversely,' rendering Greek perpereuetai ('boasts') through the Latin adverb perperam.
notes.13:5: Latin non est ambitiosa ('is not ambitious') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Greek reads ouk aschemonei ('does not act unbecomingly').
notes.13:12: Latin per speculum in aenigmate literally means 'through a mirror in a riddle,' evoking an indirect, obscure reflection as in an ancient metal mirror; the Vulgate also omits 'for' at the start of the verse.
notes.14:4: The Vulgate explicitly reads 'the church of God' (ecclesiam Dei), whereas most Greek manuscripts read simply 'the church.'
notes.14:10: The Vulgate reads 'kinds of languages' (genera linguarum) and 'in this world' (in hoc mundo), where the Greek has 'kinds of sounds' (gene phonon) and 'in the world.'
notes.14:16: Latin idiota (from Greek idiotes, also in vv. 23-24) denotes an uninstructed person or outsider lacking specialized knowledge; 'upon your blessing' (super tuam benedictionem) is a Vulgate reading where the Greek has 'at your thanksgiving' (eucharistia).
notes.14:18: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'my God' (Deo meo) and 'that I speak in the tongue of all of you' (omnium vestrum lingua loquor), omitting the comparative 'more than' (mallon) found in the Greek.
notes.14:33: The Vulgate translates Greek akatastasias ('disorder/confusion') as 'dissension' (dissensionis) and explicitly adds the verb 'I teach' (doceo), joining 'as in all the churches of the saints' to v. 33 rather than v. 34.
notes.15:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads undecim ("eleven") rather than "twelve" as in Greek manuscripts, reflecting Judas's absence after the resurrection (similarly, 15:6 reads multi, "many," rather than "most").
notes.15:23: The Clementine Vulgate distinctively includes qui ... crediderunt ("who have believed in His coming"), whereas the Greek text simply reads "those who belong to Christ at His coming."
notes.15:34: The Vulgate reads the plural adjective/vocative justi ("you righteous") rather than the Greek adverb "righteously," and renders Greek entrope ("shame") with Ecclesiastical Latin reverentiam (humbling shame or respect).
notes.15:51: A famous Vulgate-distinct reading: omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur ("we will indeed all rise, but we will not all be changed"), contrasting with the Greek text's "we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed."
notes.15:54: Following its textual tradition, the Clementine Vulgate includes only the clause about this mortal putting on immortality, omitting the parallel clause about this corruptible putting on incorruption found in most Greek manuscripts.
notes.16:2: The Vulgate reads quod ei bene placuerit ("whatever pleases him well"), whereas the Greek text has "as he may prosper."
notes.16:9: The Vulgate reads evidens ("evident"), reflecting a reading of the Greek as "clear/manifest" rather than the Greek text's "effective."
notes.16:12: The Vulgate includes vobis notum facio ("I make known to you"), absent from most Greek manuscripts, and leaves voluntas ("will") without a possessive pronoun, leaving open whether Apollos's own will or God's will is meant.
notes.16:15: The Vulgate names Fortunatus and Achaicus here alongside Stephanas (domum Stephanae, et Fortunati, et Achaici), whereas the Greek text mentions only the household of Stephanas in this verse and introduces the other two in verse 17.
notes.16:19: The Vulgate includes the closing clause apud quos et hospitor ("with them I am also lodging"), a Western reading absent from standard Greek texts, and uses the form Priscilla rather than Prisca.
notes.16:22: The Vulgate expands "the Lord" of the critical Greek text to Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum ("our Lord Jesus Christ") and retains the Aramaic expression Maran Atha ("Our Lord has come" or "Our Lord, come!"); "accursed" translates Latin anathema.
